text.p: Italian debt markets ended exhausted but happy after a fierce rally prompted by investors piling in on prospects of tougher than expected 1997 budget.

The December LIFFE future was below its latest record high of 122.50 in late trade, up 127 basis points at 121.70, but was still nearly four points up from its level of around 118 at the start of the week.

Traders said the last two days, in which Italian debt markets have rallied almost vertically, had been exhausting as buyers came in from all directions. "I'm exhausted, dead," commented one broker in London.

The February 2006 Btp ended 132 basis points higher at 107.12 after a day's high of 107.80, and the spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund wound in past the 250 basis point target cited by analysts in recent days, to close at 249.

"The budget is good -- at least on paper it should modify some ratios like debt and deficit levels in the right direction," one broker said. "But it is only on paper and it's not always certain they'll raise all the revenues."
But the end impression was Italy was whipping itself into shape to chase the goal of joining a single European currency at the outset, even if the market is sceptical of its chances.

Brokers warned the entire market is on the buy side and downward movements could be equally as spectacular if any hitch appears as the budget seeks parliamentary approval. The market had retraced earlier and one broker commented, "On the way down you can't find a single buyer."

Traders said debt auctions earlier in the day had been reasonably covered but not as much as people had expected and this had tainted the early rally. Technically, they say the market is heavily overbought and resistance in the unknown territory above December future's current record levels is hard to gauge.--Charlotte Cooper, Milan bureau +392 66129507
